name: LingoQA
intro: LingoQA 是面向自动驾驶视觉问答的 ECCV 2024 数据集与基准。论文 v4 总述为 2.8 万个四秒场景、41.99 万条问答，但论文分支表、官方 README 与当前公开 parquet 互不一致；本页显式保留这项版本漂移。评测集含 100 个留出场景、500 道独立问题和每题两条人工参考答案。官方 Lingo-Judge 对两条参考答案的 logit 取最大值，以 logit > 0 判正确并报告 500 题准确率。
build_method: 动作/场景并行构建，20+ 名内部人工双标与争议复标，独立训练 Lingo-Judge
metric: 500 题 Lingo-Judge 二元准确率（两参考答案最大 logit > 0）；Judge 验证准确率与相关性
eval_feature: 自由回答、每题两个人工参考答案、学习式真实性判别
scale: 论文总体 28K 场景/419.9K 问答；当前公开训练 parquet 为 27,999 场景/413,829 行；评测为 100 场景/500 题/1,000 条参考答案
build_method_en: Parallel Action/Scenery construction, double-labeled human evaluation with dispute relabeling, and separately trained Lingo-Judge
eval_feature_en: Free-form answers, two human references per question, learned truthfulness classification
intro_en: LingoQA is an ECCV 2024 dataset and benchmark for autonomous-driving visual question answering. Paper v4 reports a headline 28K four-second scenarios and 419.9K QA pairs, while its branch table, the official README, and the current public parquet files disagree; this page preserves that release drift explicitly. The evaluation set has 100 held-out scenarios, 500 unique questions, and two human references per question. Official Lingo-Judge takes the larger logit over the two references, marks an answer correct when that logit is greater than zero, and reports accuracy over 500 questions.
scale_en: Paper headline: 28K scenarios/419.9K QA; current public train parquet: 27,999 scenarios/413,829 rows; evaluation: 100 scenarios/500 questions/1,000 references
metric_en: 500-question Lingo-Judge binary accuracy (maximum two-reference logit > 0); Judge validation accuracy and correlation evidence

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2312.14115v4, the ECCV 2024 paper, official repository commit 39d86b14b681cbb766aaa32cbb2d4a8f5a0ed636, and Lingo-Judge Hugging Face revision a1a6e2194fd1aedaba02bde82316a6b73753d1d5. LingoQA uses a single front-facing RGB camera; each four-second span is represented by five frames at 1 Hz. Training construction has parallel Action and Scenery branches. Action starts from notable behaviour changes, operator situation/behaviour labels, and perception/vehicle metadata, then uses action/justification and question/answer-hint templates with GPT-3.5 before rebalancing action and behavioural-policy categories to at most 500 events each. Scenery densely annotates three 30-minute sessions in ELAN every second across approximately fifteen caption categories, then uses GPT-4 chain-of-thought to generate perception questions and answers, approximately 43 per scenario. Exact construction prompts, model snapshots, generation settings, and train-output QC or rejection rates are not released; the Action prose also conflicts by first saying GPT-3.5 rephrases, answers, and extends, then later saying it only rephrases. The paper headline is 28K scenarios and 419.9K QA, but Action prose reports 167,774 QA, Table 3 reports Action 267.8K plus Scenery 152.5K (420.3K total), the pinned README swaps the branch counts and ratios, and the currently served parquets contain 265,323 Action plus 148,506 Scenery rows (413,829 total across 27,999 segments). Evaluation uses 100 held-out scenarios, 500 unique human-generated questions, 20+ in-house evaluators, initial answer double-labeling without assigning the same question twice to one evaluator, manual disagreement/error review, two further labels for disputed samples, majority-semantic resolution, and two correct diverse references per question, yielding 1,000 reference rows. Judge training is separate: DeBERTa-V3 with LoRA learns from early-model predictions and human correctness labels, then adds active-learning corrections from discarded models; its train size, split, and LoRA settings are undisclosed. Fixed repository code lowercases and strips references and predictions, keeps the question as-is, serializes [CLS], Question, Answer, and Student fields with max_length 128, emits one raw logit per reference, takes the maximum over two references, marks correct when max logit is greater than zero, and reports matched-question accuracy (500 questions for a complete submission). The paper equation omits the question argument even though the prose and implementation include it. Judge evidence is 95.0% held-out accuracy and Spearman 0.950/Pearson 0.993 over 17 systems, specifically 15 models plus two human groups. Data and Judge weights are partly public under Wayve's custom non-commercial, revocable licence; Google Drive has no immutable dataset revision, candidate-VLM inference prompt/decoder/parser code is absent, and there is no official live leaderboard.
